provenance: x402 specification v2 section 5.5, Settlement and Refusal Identity Invariant, as proposed in x402-foundation/x402 pull request 3776 on branch spec/settlement-refusal-identity-invariant and not on main
the gap these cover was named by ruiruii in erc-8004/erc-8004-contracts#99 on 18 October 2026: each of the four evidence layers depends on an attempt identity that none of them defines
section 5.5 closes by referring to "the normative conformance tests in the specification repository for the required negative cases"; at the time of writing those did not exist
encodes: The second inverse trap: a reference to a signed artifact taken over a canonicalized form instead of the transmitted bytes.
description: The attempt references a separately signed offer. The reference hash matches a key-sorted rewrite of that offer rather than the bytes that were signed, so the reference names an object nobody signed. This is the exact mirror of the key-order case: there, canonicalizing is required; here, it destroys the thing. An implementation that applies one rule to both will fail one of these two vectors, and which one it fails says which half it misread.

signed_artifact_reference.note: the hash of a key-sorted rewrite, not of what was signed

limits: The checker recomputes both candidate hashes itself rather than trusting the note, so a mislabelled vector cannot pass.
